messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT — 2026-03-15T09:12:34Z — latency SLO (p95) breach on /v1/generate in eu-west1 for model-group=redwood-6b. p95 > 1200ms for the last 5m. Auto-routing triggered 42 reroutes in 5m, increased fallback activity to regional variants. Incident id: INC-1993004444

sana_oncall: I'm on pager. taking lead. starting triage: is this a model or infra regression?

mike_ops: seeing large p95 across replicas, errors low (<1%) but many requests hit the fallback path and see cold KV restore latency. metrics: p50=210ms, p95=1380ms, p99=2600ms. reroutes/sec graph: spike coincident with routing-policy change at ~09:07.

jordan_reliability: noting routing-policy rollout 09:06 by taylor_pdl — suspect hysteresis/threshold change caused flip-flop. policy id=policy-332 currently: threshold_ratio=1.05, hysteresis_s=30. too small.

taylor_pdl: yup that was my change to reduce cost from unnecessary holdouts. I misread units; thought hysteresis was minutes, it's seconds. taking ownership, rolling back now.

lee_infra: infra looks healthy (GPU utilization normal, no node restarts). KV latency spike on fallback path: redis restore + model-variant warmup ~800ms added. compounding with reroutes = observed p95 storm.

sana_oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) disable auto-fallback for impacted policy, 2) increase hysteresis, 3) pin model-variant for active capacity. Mike, can you run the commands? Jordan, validate after.

mike_ops: executing mitigations now.

```bash
# temporarily stop automatic regional fallback for policy-332
redwoodctl routing update --policy policy-332 --auto_fallback false
# increase hysteresis to 300s to prevent frequent reroutes while we stabilize
redwoodctl routing update --policy policy-332 --hysteresis 300
# pin model variant to the verified EU variant
redwoodctl model pin --model-group redwood-6b --variant redwood-6b-eu-1 --duration 15m
```

mike_ops: applied: auto_fallback=false, hysteresis=300s, variant pinned. changes propagated to control plane at 09:20.

jordan_reliability: watching metrics... reroute rate dropping. p95 trending down: 09:22 p95=480ms, 09:26 p95=310ms. good sign.

taylor_pdl: apologies for the rollout error — I reverted the change and will follow up in postmortem.

sana_oncall: customers impacted? Support, please surface any escalations.

mike_ops: Support queue: ACME corp (enterprise) reported 1200 slow requests, 5 timed out; internal ticket SUP-5643 opened. Public status: posting update now.

```text
Status update (09:28 UTC): We are investigating increased latency affecting EU region for certain model requests. Temporary mitigations in place. We will provide updates every 30 minutes.
```

jordan_reliability: baseline root cause: routing-policy hysteresis was set to 30s (too aggressive). small transient p95 blips triggered fallback; fallback introduced additional warmup latency and unreconciled variant incompatibilities causing more blips -> positive feedback loop. Also saw model-variant tag mismatch: fallback variant had slightly different KV format causing warm cache misses.

lee_infra: additional note: we should add KV warmup background prefetch on fallback paths to avoid 800ms cold restores. filing infra ticket INF-7781.

sana_oncall: mitigation status: p95 stabilized at ~240ms for 10m, reroutes negligible. leaving auto_fallback disabled for 30m while we watch.

mike_ops: confirmed: last 10m: avg reroutes/min = 0.5, p95=245ms, error-rate stable.

jordan_reliability: post-incident action items (quick list): 1) default hysteresis -> 300s for routing policies until we add smarter decay; 2) add canary gating for routing-policy changes; 3) add variant compatibility check in rollout pipeline; 4) KV warmup strategy for fallback variants. I'll own postmortem.

taylor_pdl: I'll open a PR to fix the policy rollout UI to show units clearly and add a lint check.

sana_oncall: assigning postmortem owner: jordan_reliability. I'm handing off monitoring to jordan; I'll stay available for questions. Declaring incident status: MITIGATED at 09:34 UTC. Will flip to RESOLVED after 60m of stability. :white_check_mark:

mike_ops: noting customer follow-ups: support to contact ACME with timeline and remediation.

jordan_reliability: copying runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-hysteresis|routing-hysteresis runbook>. Will include timeline, command history, and metric snapshots in the postmortem.

sana_oncall: great. thank you all for quick responses. moving to monitoring-only. leaving thread for postmortem comments.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-1993004444 status update: MITIGATED -> watching. pages closed.

jordan_reliability: postmortem checklist: add unit tests for policy unit parsing, update default hysteresis, create an alert to detect >10 reroutes/min sustained for >3m.

sana_oncall: handoff complete. oncall clear in 30m unless regression.

mike_ops: :thumbsup: saved commands for audit: `/redwoodctl history --id policy-332` includes the change and rollback entries.

incidents-bot: RESOLVED: Incident INC-1993004444 marked RESOLVED at 10:34:44Z after 60m stable.

jordan_reliability: assigning postmortem doc: DOC-1993004444-routing-hysteresis-postmortem (will link to incident page).
